content:
Olivia: Heads up — AcmePay just escalated. After the canary flip to optimus@1.5 we started seeing function-call failures from their integration. They're blocked on invoice lookups.
Maya: Can you paste the exact error they see?
Olivia: They forwarded this response from our API: `error: function_schema_validation_failed`, with detail: `args did not match schema: missing field 'customer_id'` and sometimes the model picks `search_transactions` instead of `lookup_invoice`.
Diego: Ugh — sounds like the model is calling the wrong function and/or emitting malformed JSON for the function args. Any sample request from the customer?
Olivia: Yes — here's a sanitized repro they sent (they said it worked fine before the canary):
```
POST /v1/chat
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model": "optimus",
  "version": "1.4",    # before
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Get invoice 98765 for AcmePay"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"lookup_invoice","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"invoice_id":{"type":"string"},"customer_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["invoice_id","customer_id"]}}]
}
```
Olivia: With 1.4 the model called `lookup_invoice` and returned valid args. With 1.5 it sometimes returns: `{"name":"lookup_invoice","arguments":""invoice_id: 98765""}` or chooses `search_transactions` instead.
Maya: That's consistent with model-side regression in function-calling behavior. Diego, any changes in the model tokenizer/serialization that could explain stringified args?
Diego: There were minor serialization heuristics changed in 1.5 to handle certain structured outputs — possible bug. I'll repro locally. Can someone point me to the canary rollout details?
Sasha: deploy-bot shows: optimus@1.5 canary started at 1963724400, initial traffic 5%, ramp to 20% at 1963728000.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout optimus@1.5 -> 20% traffic @ 1963728000 (initiated by eng-release).
Ken: Metrics from Console: function_call_schema_rejects baseline 0.3% -> spiked to 8.2% during canary. Latency stable. Error breakdown shows ~60% are malformed args (stringified JSON), ~40% wrong tool chosen.
Olivia: Customer impact — AcmePay is rate-limiting their users because lookup failures cascade. They asked for rollback if we can't fix in 30m.
Maya: Diego, can you reproduce with the same function schema and the model checkpoint pinned to 1.5? If so, we should confirm root cause and decide rollback.
Diego: Repro steps I'm running now — using our internal test harness to send 1000 chat requests with identical prompt+functions. I'll post results.
Diego: (10m) Quick note: I can reproduce stringified arguments about ~12% of the time locally against v1.5. Example returned content: ```{"name":"lookup_invoice","arguments":"{"invoice_id": "98765", "customer_id": "acmepay-42"}"}```
Maya: That matches logs from the customer's requests. Likely a new postprocessing pass that mistakenly double-encodes structured outputs.
Sasha: Ops question — does the fallback routing send to a compatible variant (v1.4) when schema validation fails?
Ken: Current fallback policy is by model family only; we do not auto-fallback to previous version on schema validation. We do have a canary rollback flag we can flip.
Olivia: Customer requested immediate rollback if it affects >5% of their calls. Our console shows 8.2% for them.
Maya: Two immediate options: 1) roll back canary for all users (stop 1.5 and revert to 1.4), 2) update routing for AcmePay to force v1.4 (customer-specific route) while we fix. Which is preferable?
Ken: For speed, routing AcmePay to v1.4 is fastest and lower blast radius. But we need to patch inference pipeline soon.
Diego: I can push hotfix for the serialization in the runtime — it's a 20–30min patch + quick test. However, rollback of canary is sub-5min via console.
Maya: Given customer is blocked, do the quick mitigation: route AcmePay to v1.4 and flip team-wide rollback if more customers surface after that. Olivia — can you coordinate with AcmePay on routing change?
Olivia: Reached out, they approved routing only their traffic back to v1.4. They'll share their org-id.
Sasha: I'll make the routing rule and verify traces. Ken, can you watch for other high-volume tenants with similar spikes?
Ken: On it. I'll run a quick query for tenants with function_call_schema_rejects >1% in the last 30m and ping this thread with results.
Ken: (7m) Found two more midsize customers with small spikes (1.1% and 1.8%). I'll add them to watchlist but hold off on rollback unless they go >5%.
Diego: Hotfix status: I found the double-encode in `postprocess_structured_output()` — patching now, running unit tests. ETA 25m to rollout to canary groups.
Maya: Good. Plan: 1) Apply customer-specific routing to AcmePay -> optimus@1.4 (Olivia/Sasha). 2) Diego deploys hotfix to canary (Ken watches metrics). 3) If hotfix drops schema_rejects under 0.5% for canary within 20m, we continue canary. If not, full rollback.
Olivia: Noted and told AcmePay. They're relieved by the routing change. :pray: 
Sasha: Routing rule applied for AcmePay org-id acme-org-98765 -> optimus@1.4. Traces show immediate drop in their function_call errors.
deploy-bot: Patch deployment optimus@1.5-postproc-fix started @ 1963729400 (canary subset).
Diego: Hotfix deployed to canary subset. Initial 1k requests show schema_rejects down to 0.4% and no wrong-tool selections in that sample.
Ken: Monitoring dash shows canary aggregated schema_rejects fell from 8.2% -> 0.6% across canary after patch.
Maya: Excellent. Hold on rollback. Diego, after canary stabilization (30m) we can promote patch to full rollout.
Olivia: AcmePay confirmed they can continue. I'll close the escalation after final confirmation.
Ken: I'll leave alerts on for 24h and create a follow-up issue to add auto-fallback to previous version on schema validation fails.
Maya: Agree — follow-up ticket: add version-aware fallback policy + integration test that verifies function_call arg types are well-formed after each rollout.
Olivia: Thanks everyone — great quick triage.
Diego: Leaving detailed repro and patch notes in the bug ticket.
